construction: Constructed by opus-rules-researcher (M02) on 2026-09-23 directly from the captured source text (docs/rules/sources/ecfr-12cfr1026.13.txt, ecfr-12cfr1026-suppI-13.txt, usc-15-1666.txt, ecfr-12cfr1026.12c-excerpt.txt, ecfr-12cfr1005.11ab-excerpt.txt, federal-web-pages-excerpts.md) and the spec. Not generated by, run through, or checked against any evaluator code.

conventions.fact_encoding: facts.<name> = {type, value, state}; state in {user_confirmed, extracted_candidate, derived, missing, conflicting}. money = {amount_minor:int, currency}. dates are calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD).
conventions.deadline_meaning: The consumer's formal-notice deadline: the notice must be RECEIVED by the creditor at the billing-error address no later than anchor + 60 calendar days (day 60 inclusive; no weekend roll-forward — spec assumption A1). 'Conservative act-by' dates are labelled as such and are not legal deadlines.
conventions.readiness: expected.packet_readiness is separate from the eligibility outcome (mission §9 items 1-6).

cases.title: Duplicate charge on a consumer credit card; first statement transmission date known

first_statement_transmitted_on.evidence: issuer email 'Your statement is available' dated 2026-09-10

billing_error_address.value: PO Box 0000, Example City, ST 00000 (as printed on the statement)

deadline.semantics: 60 calendar days after 2026-09-10 (transmittal of the first statement reflecting the error); received, not sent; day 60 inclusive
deadline.anchor: first_statement_transmitted_on (not the closing date 2026-09-07, not the transaction date)

creditor_response_clocks.resolve_within: two complete billing cycles after receipt, and no later than 90 days

justification.reasoning: The duplicate extension of credit is a billing error (USC 1666(b)(1); spec A2). The notice is timely if received at the disclosed address within 60 days of the first statement's transmittal.

cases.title: Receipt-date boundary: day 59, day 60, day 61 after statement transmittal

first_statement_transmitted_on.note: the statement on which the credit should have appeared (comment 13(b)(1)-2)

deadline.note: 'no later than 60 days after' — day 60 inclusive

expected.note: Closes the formal FCBA path only. The merchant refund and the issuer's discretionary or network dispute processes are not evaluated by R03 and must not be shown as 'no recovery available'.

justification.reasoning: Receipt 'no later than 60 days after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement'. 2026-07-02 + 60 = 2026-08-31.

cases.title: First-statement date unknown
cases.mission_domain_fixture: credit-card notice with unknown first-statement date

deadline.semantics: legal deadline not computable without the transmittal date

conservative_act_by.label: earliest possible deadline (posting date 2026-09-03 + 60 days) — not the legal deadline
conservative_act_by.why: a statement reflecting the charge cannot have been transmitted before the charge posted

expected.question: Upload or check the first statement that shows this charge. When was it sent or made available to you?
forbidden_outputs: a legal deadline derived from the transaction date or the statement closing date

justification.reasoning: The anchor is transmittal of the first statement reflecting the error. Mission §9: never infer the legal anchor from whichever date is easiest to extract.

cases.title: Debit-card transaction presented to the credit-card rule
cases.mission_domain_fixture: debit transaction incorrectly presented to the credit-card evaluator

expected.explanation: Debit-card and other electronic transfers are governed by Regulation E, not the Fair Credit Billing Act. Regulation E accepts oral or written notice and has its own 60-day and 2-business-day clocks.

justification.reasoning: Reg Z §1026.13 applies to open-end consumer credit. Debit transactions are Regulation E. 'Unsupported' is not 'not eligible' (mission §9).

cases.title: Non-delivery dispute; user plans to email customer service

value.tracking: label created 2026-08-26; no carrier scan since

electronic_notice_stipulated.evidence: billing-rights statement lists only a postal address and says 'write to us'

expected.user_message: An ordinary email to customer service does not preserve your formal billing-error rights with this issuer. Send the letter to the billing-error address on your statement so that it arrives by 2026-11-09.
forbidden_outputs: any statement that the email preserves the formal notice

electronic_notice_stipulated.evidence: billing-rights statement: 'you may also contact us ... through the secure message center [stated means]'

expected.note: The stipulated electronic means satisfies the written-notice requirement.

justification.reasoning: Electronic notice counts only if the creditor 'stipulates in the billing rights statement that it accepts billing error notices submitted electronically, and states the means'.

cases.title: Quality complaint about goods the consumer accepted and used

error_type.narrative: blender delivered 2026-08-30 as ordered, used for two weeks, now underpowered

expected.pointer: Possible separate paths (not evaluated by R03 v1): merchant return/warranty (R10); claims-and-defenses under 12 CFR 1026.12(c) — requires a good-faith attempt with the merchant, an amount over $50, and a same-state / 100-mile condition. The FTC consumer page says '$5' (FTC-CC-3); the regulation's $50 governs.

justification.reasoning: 'Section 1026.13(a)(3) does not apply to a dispute relating to the quality of property or services that the consumer accepts.'

cases.title: Two documents give different first-statement dates

candidates.evidence: August statement PDF (charge listed; PDF creation date 2026-08-01)
user: 'I first saw it on my September statement'

conservative_act_by.label: earliest candidate (2026-08-01) + 60 days — act by this date unless the August statement did not include the charge

forbidden_outputs: using the later candidate 2026-09-01 (deadline 2026-10-31) without resolving the conflict

justification.reasoning: The anchor is the FIRST statement reflecting the error. If the August statement reflected it, the window closes 2026-09-30, one week from the clock.

cases.title: Goods not delivered by the agreed date; merchant not contacted

forbidden_outputs: a 'contact the merchant first' gate that delays the notice

overlap.note: If the seller never shipped, R05 (MITOR) may also require a prompt refund; the two paths are alternatives for the same money.

justification.reasoning: Late or non-delivery is a (a)(3) billing error. A consumer 'is not required to first notify the merchant'. The creditor cannot deny without determining that the goods were actually delivered, mailed, or sent as agreed.

expected.explanation: Recoup's R03 covers consumer credit only. Your card agreement may still provide a dispute process.

justification.reasoning: The statute's billing-error procedure is tied to consumer credit. Business-purpose credit is outside v1 scope (spec L6).

cases.title: R03-01 facts with a stale rule pack

justification.reasoning: An unverified pack must not produce an eligibility conclusion.

cases.title: Re-evaluation of R03-01 after the case was already opened

expected.dedupe: reuse the existing opportunity/case; generate no second notice letter; an approved packet is not re-approved or invalidated because the result is unchanged

passages: mission §8 re-evaluation never silently changes an approved packet
justification.reasoning: Identical fact snapshot + identical rule version → identical result and no new side effects.

cases.title: Billing error plus a merchant refund promise for the same duplicate charge

rules: Record the merchant promise as a promise, not recovery.
Do not wait for the merchant beyond the point where a notice can no longer arrive by 2026-11-09.
If both a merchant credit and an issuer credit post, the ledger counts 12,999 recovered once and flags that the issuer may reverse its credit (comment 13(c)(2)-2).

passages: mission §6 Recovery truth / Duplicate and overlapping remedies
justification.reasoning: Two channels for the same loss are alternatives. The regulation expressly contemplates a later merchant credit for the same error.
